subject: Clarify billing scenario mapping & rounding examples
messages:
From: Dana Lee <dana@hypershelf.com>

Subject: Billing: long-context flows + rounding/minimums (examples attached)

Hey Sean,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We love the throughput—one open question from procurement: how do you actually account for billing when we have a mix of very short assistant calls and occasional 50k+ token retrieval sessions? They asked for a few concrete invoice-line style examples so they can map to our PO. I attached a small CSV with representative sessions from last month.

Specific asks:
- When a single conversation has multi-turn back-and-forth plus a long document load, do you bill per request or aggregate to a conversation-level bucket?
- How do you round partial tokens (e.g., 12.3 tokens) and how are minimums applied?
- Any examples showing the effect of a 1% discount vs a negotiated volume discount on the unit math would help.

Can you send a short mapping with 2–3 scenarios so Purchasing can sign off?

Thanks,
Dana
Dana Lee
Head of Integrations, HyperShelf
Dana@hypershelf.com

Attachment: hypershelf_usage_sample.csv (CSV, 28KB)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Lee <dana@hypershelf.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing: long-context flows + rounding/minimums (examples attached)

Hi Dana — appreciate the file.

Short answer: we meter at the request level but provide conversation-level aggregation on the invoice; rounding and minimums are applied per our billing quantum. Below are three concise scenarios mapped to invoice-style lines (I kept the math inline). Vanessa and Ben are cc'd in case you want a pilot concession.

Scenario A — Short interactive assistant (many tiny turns)
- Usage: 120 requests, average request = 45 tokens encoded + 55 tokens generated = 100 tokens/request
- Quantum: 8-token rounding up (our current backend quantum for efficiency) => 100 tokens -> round to 104 tokens/request
- Billable tokens: 120 * 104 = 12,480 tokens
- Invoice line (hosted): 12,480 tokens @ $0.00035/token = $4.37

Scenario B — Mixed conversation with long document load (single request loads ~51,400 tokens, subsequent turns small)
- Request 1: load doc + prompt = 51,432 tokens -> rounded up to nearest quantum => 51,432 -> 51,440
- Follow-ups: 8 subsequent small requests at 320 tokens actual -> round to 320 -> 320 (already multiple of quantum)
- Billable tokens: 51,440 + (8 * 320) = 54,000 tokens
- Invoice line: 54,000 tokens @ $0.00035 = $18.90

Scenario C — Streaming/partial-output scenario with fractional token accounting
- Streamed generation produced 2,345.6 generated tokens (we bill generated tokens as integers after rounding to quantum)
- Rounded generated: 2,345.6 -> round up to 2,352 (next multiple of 8)
- If below a per-request minimum (e.g., 64 tokens), we apply the per-request minimum instead.
- Example: a tiny stream that would round to 56 -> per-request minimum becomes 64.

Discount examples (applied on token unit price):
- List price: $0.00035/token
- 1% discount: $0.0003465/token -> scenario B delta = 54,000 * (0.00035 - 0.0003465) = $0.189
- 15% volume discount (pilot): $0.0002975/token -> scenario B = 54,000 * $0.0002975 = $16.065

I'll attach a two-line proposed terms PDF with a suggested pilot concession if you want faster approval.

If this format works, I can produce a one-page PDF that maps to your PO line items exactly.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

Attachments: proposed_tier_terms_v2.pdf
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Billing: long-context flows + rounding/minimums (examples attached)

Logging a succinct internal note and adding a pilot-friendly option. Key operational points to confirm for HyperShelf:

1) Metering granularity and quantum rationale
- We meter per request at the time of execution; for efficiency and kernel alignment we round up to an 8-token quantum. That quantum is applied to input and output tokens separately.

2) Conversation aggregation on invoice
- Although metered per request, we roll up lines per conversation id on monthly invoices for readability (invoice shows total tokens for the conversation). This keeps procurement happy while preserving accurate metering for throttling and limits.

3) Minimums and floor behavior
- Per-request minimum token floor = 64 tokens for hosted API by default (this protects against very small calls being charged below the baseline).
- For Dedicated contracts we can lower the floor to 16 tokens with a commensurate seat/commit.

4) Example invoice-format (CSV line per conversation):
- conversation_id, start_ts, end_ts, billable_tokens, unit_price, line_amount
- CV-20260901-0001, 2026-09-01T08:01Z,2026-09-01T08:12Z,54000,$0.00035,$18.90

Pilot concession proposal (for approval):
- 12-week pilot: apply 15% volume discount on billable tokens for first $25k of spend; reduce per-request minimum to 32 tokens for the pilot; apply one-time credit for any rounding delta > $50 in a billing month.

Operational note for billing engineers (Ben): please confirm that we can expose the rounding quantum per-API key in the billing export CSV so HyperShelf can reconcile easily.

-Vanessa
